title: Continuous compatibility and fallback decision layer for pinned models
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem statement:
Customers can pin model versions for strict reproducibility. When the pinned model becomes unavailable, degraded, or deprecated, we need a deterministic, observable, and auditable fallback system that: (1) preserves API contract and structured outputs where possible, (2) minimizes latency and cost regressions, and (3) provides clear deprecation notices and migration paths in the Console and API.

Goal:
Build a fallback decision layer (FDL) that runs upstream of the router and uses a compatibility score + policy table to select fallbacks for pinned versions. The FDL must support region-aware fallbacks, model-variant substitutions (quantized/reduced-seq models), and staged deprecation workflows. It should publish performance profiles for variants to Console and the model catalog to enable deterministic trade-offs.

Design summary (high-level):
- Compatibility scoring: compute an ordinal score for candidate fallback variants using factors: API schema match (structured output), tokenizer compatibility, performance profile (p50/p95 latency for typical seq lengths), soft-quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE/emb cosine baseline), and feature flags (tools/function-calling support).
- Precedence rules (evaluated in order):
  1) Same-region, same-model-family, highest compatibility score (prefer exact schema match).
  2) Same-region, model-variant (e.g., int8/4-bit quantized) with compatibility >= 0.85 and <=10% median latency increase.
  3) Cross-region compatible variant within 100ms added tail latency budget with higher priority if SLA allows.
  4) Tiered fallbacks: if no compatible variant, route to a higher-capacity hosted fallback pool with explicit rate-limited compensation and user-visible deprecation header.
- Deprecation handling: support three modes: silent-deprecation (no routing change; only Console warning), staged-deprecation (traffic gradually migrated based on canary rules + compatibility score), and forced-deprecation (no longer allowed to pin; automatic mapping to recommended variant with audit log).
- Performance profile publishing: whenever a variant is onboarded/published, the onboarding flow must compute and store profile data (latency buckets, token throughput, cost per 1k tokens, memory footprint) and surface an auto-generated compatibility vector used by FDL.

Acceptance criteria:
- FDL service with idempotent decision API (GET /fallback-decision?pin=... returns ordered candidates) implemented and covered by unit/integration tests.
- Console displays per-pin fallback chain and compatibility scores for each candidate variant.
- Rollout policy UI allows customers to select deprecation mode per-pin or globally.
- End-to-end e2e test demonstrates graceful fallback: simulate complete loss of a pinned GPU pool in a region and validate traffic migrates to same-region quantized variant with <2x latency regression for 95% of requests.
- Audit trail entries for every automatic fallback and deprecation event (linkable to the customer’s audit logs).

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Conservative compatibility threshold (0.85) risks favoring cross-region fallbacks with latency cost; lower threshold risks quality regressions. We propose to A/B test 0.80/0.85/0.90 buckets in runtime-1.24 beta.
- Cost surface: preferring hosted fallbacks may increase unit cost; we must expose expected cost delta in Console before applying forced-deprecation mappings.
- Implementation complexity: compute-heavy compatibility scoring needs precomputed vectors to avoid runtime overhead — will reuse existing performance-profile publishing pipeline.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Data plane: add compatibility vector to model metadata and extend onboarding pipeline to compute performance profiles (ENG-19844 dependent).
2) Decision layer: implement FDL service (stateless) with configurable precedence rules and feature flags.
3) Router integration: add evaluation hook in routing tier to call FDL when a pin is unreachable or flagged deprecated.
4) Console & API: surface fallback chains and deprecation mode controls; publish performance profile UI.
5) SRE & Testing: chaos test to simulate regional outages, load test to validate decision latency under 1000rps.

Rollback and safety:
- Feature gated behind runtime-1.24 feature flag for 2 weeks; default to existing fallback behavior.
- Rate-limited rollout: initial canary 5% of tenants increasing to 100% after metrics.
- Kill-switch in Console to revert to legacy pin-fail behavior.

Notes on observability:
- Emit FDL.DecisionTaken event with fields: pin_key, selected_candidate, reason_code, compatibility_score, latency_estimate (published to event-stream).
- Link decision events to per-tenant audit logs and to Console incident timeline.

Related artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/FDL+PRD, onboarding spec: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ModelOnboardSpec, perf harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness, runtime PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4589
acceptance_criteria: FDL returns deterministic ordered candidates for a pinned model key
Console shows fallback chain + compatibility scores visible in model catalog and pin settings
E2E failure test: regional GPU pool loss causes migration per precedence rules with verified latency/cost bounds
Audit logs for each automatic fallback and deprecation are generated and queryable
